MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 9, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on May 9, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 5, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that the City Manager and members of the City Council made
  a blatant effort to pursue a politically motivated lawsuit against her.

City Council Minutes  1  May 9, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council considered a personnel item in Closed
Session. The Council received information and provided some instruction but no reportable action
occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the
  Quarter" Lance Corporal Marvel A. Salazar and "Noncommissioned Officer of the
  Quarter" Corporal Mollie Matyevich.

 P2.  Recognize the Bathgate Elementary School Team "5 Pomeranians in a Walnut
  Tornado" for Placing First in the Destination Imagination Competition in
  Sacramento

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of recognition to the Bathgate Elementary School
  Destination Imagination Team.

 P3.  Proclaim May through October, 2017, for "Drowning Prevention and Awareness"

  Mayor Bucknum presented the proclamation and Battalion Chief John Abel shared a
  video and statistics on drownings in Mission Viejo.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Jennifer Heinen, Laguna Niguel: introduced herself as the new Executive Director of the Mission
Viejo Family YMCA and outlined upcoming programs and activities at the YMCA.

Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: announced that she is on the Board of Directors for Community Action
Partnership of Orange County which will hold two public forums for the purpose of looking at
community needs. The meetings will be held on May 10 at 12:00 p.m. at the Murray Community
Center in Mission Viejo and on the evening of May 15 at Family Assistance Ministries.

City Council Minutes  2  May 9, 2017
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 11 and 20 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles

2.  City Council Minutes

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay noted that the dollar

  ($1,517,359.81.00 and $758,679.91) for Council consideration and approval.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  approve Fourth Amendment to the existing maintenance contract with Vandergeest
  Landscape Care, Inc. for the period July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2019, to increase the
  contract amount by an amount not to exceed $1,517,359.81.00; and (2) authorize staff to
City Council Minutes  6  May 9, 2017
   issue a purchase order to Vandergeest Landscape Care, Inc. for the period July 1, 2017,
  through June 30, 2018, in an amount not to exceed $758,679.91, pending adoption of the
  2017-2019 budget by the City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  NOES:  None

20.  Alicia Parkway Corridor Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP 16227)

  Mayor Bucknum announced that she pulled this item from the Consent Calendar to allow
  for a conversation about what the traffic signal synchronization plan entails. She asked if
  the collisions that occur at Alicia and Jeronimo can be addressed.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report and noted that this is a
  regional, multi-jurisdictional project to synchronize signals along the corridor. He noted
  that improvements are recommended at the Alicia/Jeronimo intersection as well as
  Alicia/Fabricante and Jeronimo/Acero to reduce congestion and improve efficiency.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to (1) authorize
  staff to remove the west leg crosswalk on Alicia Parkway at its intersection with Jeronimo
  Road; and (2) authorize staff to implement operational improvements at the intersections
  of Alicia Parkway and Via Fabricante and Jeronimo Road and Acero Road as
  recommended in the Traffic Operational Improvements Study.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

23.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Renovation ~ CIP 14325

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  approve Contract Amendment No. 3 to Construct 1 One Corp., in an amount not to exceed
  $119,702.45 for unknown field conditions;(2) adopt Resolution 17-17 Amending CIP
  14325 Marguerite Aquatics Complex Budget by $50,000.00.

City Council Minutes  7  May 9, 2017
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None

24.  First Amendment to the Franchise Agreement for Solid Waste Services and Review
  of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates

  Environmental Program Administrator Denise Matson presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 17-18 Approving the First Amendment to the Franchise Agreement for
  Solid Waste Services between the City of Mission Viejo and U.S. Waste of California, dba

  First Amendment on Behalf of the City; and (2) adopt Resolution 17-19 Approving the
  Proposed Trash Rate Adjustments for Residential (3.7% Increase from $13.12 to $13.60

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None

NEW BUSINESS

25.  FY 2017-18 Law Enforcement Services Estimate

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report and answered the City Council Members
  questions. The Council commended staff and the Sheriff's Department for their
  resourcefulness in reducing costs as much as possible and reiterated the City Council's
  dedication to public safety.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

26.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

27.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Transit Master Plan Workshops

City Council Minutes  8  May 9, 2017
   Mayor Bucknum appointed Council Member Raths to participate in the Orange County
  Transportation Authority (OCTA) Transit Master Plan Workshops on May 17, 2017, from
  8:30 to 10:30 a.m., and two future workshops in fall 2017 and spring 2018.

STAFF REPORTS

29.  Legislative Update

  The City council received an update on pending legislation from Cori Williams of
  Townsend and Associates.

  By consensus, the Council took a position of opposition to AB 1250 and directed the Mayor
  to send a letter to notify the appropriate parties.

28.  Independent Accountant’s Reports on Applying Agreed-Upon Procedures

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report and answered
  the City Council Member's questions.

  The City Council received and filed the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

30.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell discussed his attendance at the South Orange County Watershed
Management District meeting which he attended on behalf of Council Member Kelley who had
another obligation. He said it was an interesting meeting but he did not have anything of substance
to report. Council Member Goodell reported that Max, the dog he and his family adopted from the
Mission Viejo Animal Services Center, is doing very well and his family is having a good time
with him.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at the Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) General Assembly. At the conference, profiles of each jurisdiction were
presented and she received one for the City of Mission Viejo. She noted that the profiles are
available online at www.scag.ca.gov for those who would like information on population, retail
sales, where people who live in the City work, demographics, public health and other useful
City Council Minutes  9  May 9, 2017
 facts. She noted that the SCAG Board adopted the 2017-18 Budget and Membership Assessment
Schedule and Margaret Finlay of the City of Duarte was elected President for the upcoming year.
Council Member Kelley discussed the recent Arts Alive event which she said was wonderful and
seems to get better and better every year. She commended staff for pulling off a huge two-day
event and for the seamless cleanup when the winds wreaked havoc the night before. She announced
that the Community of Character student subcommittee has planned a special event on May 20
from 6:00 to 9:00 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at city hall. It is a Teen Survival Guide presentation
designed to help prepare 8th graders for some of the social challenges they may encounter in high
school. Council Member Kelley said that she will miss the next Council Meeting as she will be
visiting her youngest son who is graduating from seminary and whose wife is expecting their fourth
child. She also announced that the Character word for month of May is Moral Courage and the
Character film is Gandhi. It will be shown on May 21 at 2:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at city
hall. In closing, Council Member Kelley read a quote about moral courage: "Be brave enough to
stand up for what is right, although it may not be popular or easy, and even if you stand alone."

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths said that he too attended the Arts Alive festival and staff did a great job on
the event. He announced that there will be a grand opening for the Orange County Tax Assessor's
satellite office which is on the 2nd floor of Mission Viejo’s City Hall. The event will be held on
May 23 from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. and Tax Collector Claude Parish will be present. Council Member
Raths discussed his recent meeting with the new Chamber of Commerce Executive Director, Doug
Zielasko. The Chamber is planning a new campaign in the summer to promote buying local, hiring
local and to try and increase sales for Mission Viejo businesses. He said it would be a good time
for the City to consider waving the fee for special signs/large banners and asked that staff return
at a future meeting so the Council can consider waiving those fees. In closing, Council Member
Raths reminded his colleagues and the community that the Rotary Club’s Texas Hold ‘Em
fundraiser will be held on June 10, 2017, at 5:00 p.m. at the Murray Community Center.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs announced that he attended the Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) conference in Palm Desert primarily because the Toll Road Authority was
awarded an outstanding achievement in sustainability award. He said it was fun to be part of the
group that was there to receive the award. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked if any of his colleagues
would like to be an alternate for the Association of California Cities-Orange County Legislative
Committee and Council Member Raths volunteered.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum thanked Council Members Raths and Goodell for covering at the Mayor's Prayer
Breakfast and representing the City Council, and Council Member Goodell for representing the
City at the National Day of Prayer service. She announced that it is National Nurses Week and she
thanked the city's nurses for all that they do. Mayor Bucknum shared that last week she presented
a proclamation at the Elks Club about National Youth Week. She noted that the Elks have given
City Council Minutes  10  May 9, 2017
 out numerous awards and she thanked the members for the many good things they do for the
community. She also thanked staff for scrambling to get things cleaned up after high winds caused
damage at the Arts Alive Festival setup and she said it was an honor for her to give out awards to
the amazing artists. Mayor Bucknum discussed her attendance at the Concert on the Courts last
weekend at the Marguerite Tennis Pavilion and La Paz School's jazz concert at the Murray
Community Center. She said there is so much going on in the City and it is all about arts, music
and family.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:03 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, May 23, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.
